articles.title: ESPHome lets voice devices listen and play at the same time
articles.dek: Makers can run a microphone and speaker together even when they share one digital audio port.
body: ESPHome adds simultaneous recording and playback for devices whose microphone and speaker share one I²S digital audio port. Previously, starting one side locked out the other, preventing a device with a single audio codec from recording while it played sound.

Remco van Essen adds an optional full-duplex configuration with matching audio clocks and formats. It supports a standard microphone and speakers using an external digital-to-analogue converter; multiple speakers can share the connection, but only one plays at a time. Resamplers can adapt the shared format for voice processing or incoming music.

[resampler] Add resampler microphone platform

articles.title: Home Assistant opens one home for every kind of contributor
articles.dek: The new contributor website starts with small steps for translators, testers, writers and developers, while preserving old links.
body: Home Assistant opens contributors.home-assistant.io as a single starting point for people who want to help, whether they write code, translate, test betas, improve documentation, design or answer community questions. Each area begins with a concrete first contribution, and the getting-started guide puts paths that need no code first.

In the launch post, Franck Nijhof describes a beginner’s GitHub guide that walks through a first change in the browser, a glossary explaining old and current terms, and a roadmap guide following an idea through to completed work. The design section lets readers try actual Home Assistant interface components while reading their guidance.

The site replaces the developer, design and data portals. Existing links and developer-blog posts keep their destinations through redirects, so bookmarks and older guides remain useful. Search runs in the browser without sending the query away.

articles.title: ESPHome keeps hidden controls out of its web API
articles.dek: Direct addresses stop bypassing the choice to keep low-level entities internal.
body: ESPHome’s web server stops reading and controlling internal entities through a direct address unless the owner explicitly enables them. Those entities were already hidden from the web page, but their names could still be used to reach them through the API.

That matters when a maker hides a raw relay behind a higher-level switch that adds a timer, an interlock or automatic shutoff: calling the relay directly bypasses that wrapper. Existing scripts that intentionally use such addresses must explicitly expose internal entities or make the chosen entity public. The correction is sebo-b’s first contribution to ESPHome.

pullRequests.title: [web_server] Do not match internal entities by URL unless include_internal is set

articles.title: ESPHome controls Haier water heaters through a local connection
articles.dek: A wired replacement for the Wi-Fi module supplies temperatures, modes and hot-water status.
body: ESPHome adds local control for Haier hOn water heaters by connecting to the appliance’s serial interface in place of its original Wi-Fi module. The implementation was tested on a Haier VH3W and controls power, operating mode and target temperature.

The connection checks the appliance every five seconds and can report its second temperature zone, estimated heating time and available hot water. A command is treated as complete only after the heater confirms it in a status message. Contributor TheLexus supplies the implementation and companion guide in their first contribution to ESPHome.

pullRequests.title: [haier_water_heater] Initial water-heater implementation tested with Haier VH3W
[haier_water_heater] Added documentation for Haier water heater

articles.title: Music Assistant chooses higher-quality copies across music sources
articles.dek: An optional quality threshold finds a better copy across your music sources, even when an album or playlist prefers its original source.
body: Music Assistant adds an optional quality threshold for choosing which copy of a song plays. An old MP3 rip can give way to a higher-quality version from a connected music service, including inside an album, playlist or folder and when local files are preferred.

The setting starts off. Listeners can ask for high-bitrate compressed audio, lossless audio or high-resolution audio. When preparing a track, Music Assistant prefers a copy meeting that threshold, or the closest better copy it knows. If needed, it searches other services for a match. The first song can wait up to five seconds; later songs are prepared while the current song plays.

This adds an explicit exception to the source-preserving playback reported on October 14. Copies whose quality is unknown are left alone, and audiobooks and podcasts keep the account they started from. Marcel van der Veldt supplies the setting and a guide to how the source choices interact.

articles.title: Home Assistant opens a Python console for live troubleshooting
articles.dek: Developers can inspect a running system in the Tools panel, with explicit setup and administrator access.
body: Home Assistant adds a Python console for inspecting and debugging a running installation from its Tools panel. Developers can run code against the live system, expand results as an object tree and use completion and signature hints without opening a separate Python session.

Franck Nijhof makes the console an explicit YAML opt-in for administrators. Each user accepts a warning before running code, and execution is logged with the person responsible. Sessions belong to each user and browser tab and remain available for thirty minutes after disconnecting.
The console works with live internals, so running code can change the installation. Completion and signature hints themselves do not execute user code.

articles.title: ESPHome draws rotated displays faster with less memory
articles.dek: An ESP32-S3 test cuts peak redraw time from 193 to 125 milliseconds.
body: ESPHome reduces the extra copying needed to draw rotated RGB displays, helping makers use screens in portrait orientation with less memory and shorter redraws. The change writes rotated pixels straight to the display buffer instead of creating a separate rotated copy.

On Hasan Khalil’s ESP32-S3 CrowPanel with an 800-by-480 display and a tuned 12.5% drawing buffer, peak rendering time fell from 193.4 to 125.1 milliseconds and average time from 24.3 to 17.8 milliseconds. The test also eliminated a 96-kilobyte rotation buffer. This is his first contribution to ESPHome.

pullRequests.title: [mipi_rgb] direct-to-PSRAM rotated blitting for hardware rotation

articles.title: Home Assistant automations can react to updates and restart requests
articles.dek: New triggers distinguish a changed version from an ordinary restart and expose pending maintenance.
body: Home Assistant gives automations direct triggers for a completed update and for requests to restart Home Assistant or reboot its host. A routine can react to these events without maintaining template sensors to compare versions or infer a pending restart.

The update trigger fires after startup only when the version differs from the last run, and includes both version numbers. A restart request identifies the integrations asking for it. Separate conditions let routines check a request that already existed when the automation was enabled; enabling it does not fire an old request again.

Add homeassistant.updated trigger

articles.title: ESPHome stops corrupted meter readings inflating energy totals
articles.dek: Invalid Teleinfo values are skipped instead of looking like a meter reset.
body: ESPHome stops turning unreadable Teleinfo meter values into zero. For an accumulated energy reading, that false zero could make Home Assistant treat the next valid reading as a new meter cycle and add the meter’s entire total to its statistics again.

Frédéric Metrich changes the parser to warn and skip values that are not numbers, while preserving genuine zero readings. This prevents one source of artificial consumption spikes without requiring a custom filter.

articles.title: Z-Wave JS drops invalid reports before they disrupt the network
articles.dek: A malformed test status previously triggered a full Home Assistant Z-Wave reload.
body: Z-Wave JS rejects out-of-range test-status values before passing them to connected applications. The correction follows a report from a 184-device network where an unsolicited status value caused Home Assistant to reload its entire Z-Wave connection.
The driver drops the invalid report before it reaches connected applications. The correction is derekcentrico’s first contribution to Z-Wave JS, with review by AlCalzone.

pullRequests.title: fix(cc): reject invalid statuses in Powerlevel Test Node Report

articles.title: Home Assistant Green’s reset guide replaces a failing installer
articles.dek: The older SD-card image cannot resolve the download address after a DNS trust-key change.
body: Home Assistant Green’s SD-card reset guide points to a new installer after the older image stopped resolving the address needed to download Home Assistant OS. The support report traces the failure to the October 11 change of a DNS root trust key, rather than the customer’s choice of DNS server.

The linked October 15 installer carries a newer resolver with both trust keys. Support checked the download links and sent the replacement to two affected customers, but had not yet confirmed a completed reset on Green hardware. Anyone following a saved copy of the guide should use its current installer link.

pullRequests.title: Green SD card reset: link the 20261015 installer

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps OpenRGB lights connected across computer restarts
articles.dek: Stable identities prevent duplicates and preserve light groups when the computer reassigns connection paths.
body: Home Assistant stops OpenRGB devices that report a serial number from appearing as new devices when a computer changes their connection paths. Previously, restarts or reconnecting a peripheral could leave the old entity unavailable and silently remove its light from groups.

Tristyn Russelo preserves existing records while replacing the unstable part of their identity, tested across real computer restarts with Razer peripherals. Devices without a reported serial number can still duplicate, and pre-existing conflicting duplicates are left alone.

pullRequests.title: Fix OpenRGB duplicating devices when the connection path changes

articles.title: Music Assistant’s phone player goes silent when you press Pause
articles.dek: Buffered audio stops locally even when the server connection has failed.
body: Music Assistant’s mobile app stops its own audio immediately when someone presses Pause, even if the server cannot be reached. Previously, the button could change appearance while buffered sound continued for minutes, waiting for a server response.

Andrii Mitnovych makes the phone discard the waiting audio and stay silent through reconnecting until playback is deliberately resumed or the server confirms it has stopped. A queued Pause stays ahead of a later Play so the server starts a fresh stream.

pullRequests.title: Silence the local player at once on a local pause

articles.title: Home Assistant schedules Besen charging on the charger itself
articles.dek: A start time and duration replace the immediate, unlimited session offered by the Charge switch.
body: Home Assistant adds a Besen action that schedules charging up to twenty-four hours ahead and optionally limits how long the session lasts. The schedule is stored on the charger rather than requiring Home Assistant to send the start command at that moment.

Turning the Charge switch off cancels the schedule. A start time without a timezone uses Home Assistant’s configured timezone. The existing switch continues to start an immediate session without a time limit.

pullRequests.title: Add Besen start charging action
Document Besen start charging action

articles.title: Home Assistant recovers iCloud accounts waiting for new terms
articles.dek: An explicit acceptance step replaces unknown errors and repeated requests for an already valid code.
body: Home Assistant asks an iCloud owner to accept Apple’s updated terms when those terms block signing in. Previously, setup could fail with an unknown error or repeatedly ask for a verification code that was already valid.

Existing connections enter the same recovery flow when Apple requires new terms. Acceptance is sent only after the owner agrees, and a failed acceptance produces a specific error instead of repeating the prompt. This also helps accounts whose owners have no Apple device offering the terms.

pullRequests.title: Handle Apple's updated iCloud terms in the config flow

articles.title: Home Assistant accepts sign-ins through Tailscale and public IP addresses
articles.dek: The login flow recognizes the address used to reach the interface instead of rejecting its own client.
body: Home Assistant fixes sign-ins opened through a Tailscale address, public IPv4 address or global IPv6 address. These routes could fail with Invalid client id because the login check accepted domain names and local addresses but rejected the interface’s own address.

The correction accepts an address whose protocol, host and port match the request, including the forwarded address from a trusted proxy. Existing checks binding the authorization response to the client’s redirect addresses remain in place.

pullRequests.title: Allow IndieAuth client_ids matching the request netloc

articles.title: Home Assistant restores Blink sign-ins rejected before password checks
articles.dek: Each installation keeps its own identity instead of sending a shared value the camera service rejects.
body: Home Assistant repairs Blink sign-ins that fail before the service checks the password. A shared device identifier was rejected by Blink’s authorization and token-refresh endpoints for affected installations.

The connection creates and preserves an identifier for each installation and removes the rejected old value during migration. Existing setups can recover at their next setup without a forced sign-in. The contributor observed that the rejection did not affect every installation. This is Sam Artuso’s first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

pullRequests.title: Fix Blink setup broken by OAuth hardware_id rejection (HTTP 406)

articles.title: Home Assistant saves the current room settings into KNX scenes
articles.dek: Compatible actuators can learn a scene directly from an automation.
body: Home Assistant adds an action that tells KNX actuators to save their current settings into a selected KNX scene. It works with scenes configured through the interface or YAML and takes the address and scene number from that scene.
The devices must support scene learning. Saving does not activate the scene or change its displayed activation state.

pullRequests.title: Add knx.save_scene action
Document the knx.save_scene action

articles.title: Nature Remo brings its sensor readings to Home Assistant
articles.dek: The new connection starts with readings through Nature’s cloud service; remote controls remain outside this first step.
body: Home Assistant adds a built-in Nature Remo connection for reading sensors through the Japanese smart-home platform’s cloud service. This first version supplies setup and sensor support, rather than the platform’s complete set of remote-control functions.

Yuki Fujisaki verified the implementation on owned hardware spanning four generations of hubs and a smart meter in his first contribution to Home Assistant Core. A separate custom integration already offers a fuller set of functions; those capabilities should not be assumed for this initial built-in connection.

pullRequests.title: Add Nature Remo integration

articles.title: Music Assistant’s sound-based discovery starts with large libraries
articles.dek: Preparing similarity indexes moves into the background instead of repeatedly blocking startup.
body: Music Assistant prevents its Sonic Similarity provider from repeatedly failing to start on large libraries. Preparing the data for sound-based discovery no longer runs inside startup steps with two- and five-minute limits, which could time out and repeat the same large database reads.

Chris moves that preparation to a background task. Similar-track requests remain unavailable until the initial index is ready, and a failed rebuild appears in the provider’s status and is retried hourly. One report involved 88,000 tracks and a 2.6 GB analysis database.

pullRequests.title: Keep the Sonic Similarity index builds off the provider load path

articles.title: Home Assistant switches inputs on compatible Panasonic Viera televisions
articles.dek: A tested 2017 television reports its selected input and accepts direct changes.
body: Home Assistant adds input selection for Panasonic Viera televisions that expose the optional input-control service. The media player lists the television’s inputs, reports the current one and waits for the television to confirm a requested switch.
The contributor verified listing, reporting and switching on a 2017 TX-55EZ950E. Televisions without the required service keep their existing controls without receiving the input selector.

pullRequests.title: Add input source selection to Panasonic Viera
